marks.gloss_en: R' Yose b. R' Chanina: one who waited for his fellow merits these blessings -- 'if only you had listened to My commandments, your peace would be as a river... your seed as the sand'
Abba Binyamin: had the eye been given leave to see, no creature could stand before the demons
Abaye: they are more numerous than we are, and stand over us like the ridge of earth around a furrow
Rav Huna: every one of us has a thousand at his left and ten thousand at his right
Rava: the crowding at the kalla is from them; fatigued knees are from them; the Sages' clothes wearing out is from their rubbing; bruised feet are from them
one who wishes to know of them: sift fine ashes around his bed, and in the morning he sees something like chicken tracks
Abba Binyamin: a person's prayer is heard only in the synagogue -- 'to hear the song and the prayer': where there is song, there let prayer be
R' Yitzchak: the Holy One is present in the synagogue -- 'God stands in the congregation of God'
the Shekhina is with ten who pray -- from the same verse, 'God stands in the congregation of God'
the Shekhina is with three who sit in judgment -- 'in the midst of the judges He judges'
the Shekhina is with two who sit and engage in Torah -- 'then those who feared the Lord spoke one with another, and the Lord listened'
Rav Ashi: 'and those who think upon His name' -- one who intended to do a mitzva and was prevented, Scripture credits him as if he had done it
the Shekhina is even with one who sits and engages in Torah -- 'in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come to you and bless you'
two: their words are written in the book of remembrance; one: his words are not written
judgment too is Torah (and not merely peace-keeping in the world)
for ten the Shekhina comes ahead of them; for three, only once they are seated
ותניא, רבי אליעזר הגדול אומר: אלו תפילין שבראש -- the verse's 'name of the Lord called upon you' is the head-tefillin, so the verse says tefillin are Israel's strength
tefillin are strength for Israel
אי הכי, נפישי להו טובי בתי? -- if so, there are too many compartments: five verses beyond ומי כעמך, but a head-tefillin has four
אלא -- the two 'great nation' verses, which resemble each other, share a compartment; אשריך ישראל shares one with ומי כעמך; או הנסה and ולתתך עליון take one each: four compartments

the arrangement: 'for who is a great nation' and 'and who is a great nation', which resemble each other, in one compartment; 'happy are you, Israel' and 'who is like Your people Israel' in one; 'or has God attempted' in one; 'and to elevate you' in one
the Holy One, blessed be He, wears tefillin
'by His right hand' is the Torah -- 'from His right hand, a fiery law for them' (Deut 33:2)
what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world?
and is the Holy One glorified through the glory of Israel?
'you made Me one entity' -- from 'Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One' (Deut 6:4)
that accounts for one compartment; what is in the other compartments?

Rav Ashi: the other compartments hold 'for who is a great nation' (Deut 4:7), 'and who is a great nation' (4:8), 'happy are you, Israel' (33:29), 'or has God attempted' (4:34), 'and to elevate you' (26:19)
